inputs.label: Unused Flipper Column Lower Right End-of-Stroke (81)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPEOSBIT = 0x01, published at 81 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. locals.flipMask carries this end-of-stroke bit only when hw.flippers sets FLIP_EOS (implied by FLIP_SOL), and FLIP6364 = FLIP_SWNO(63,64) sets neither, so core_updateSw neither synthesizes it nor copies it anywhere: PinMAME models no end-of-stroke switch on this machine. A host write survives in the column, but the ROM cannot read it there: s11.c's pia4a_r reads the switch matrix only through core_getSwCol with an eight-bit column strobe, which reaches columns 1-8.

inputs.label: Lower Right Flipper Button (PinMAME Flipper Column)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPBUTBIT = 0x02, published at 82 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. This is the lower right cabinet flipper button as the ROM receives it. The driver declares FLIP6364 = FLIP_SWNO(63,64) with no FLIP_SOL, so with keyboard handling off (the LibPinMAME default) core_updateSw reads this bit as the host wrote it and, on every update, copies it into matrix switch 64 through core_setSw and fabricates the synthetic 45/46 flipper outputs from it while the switched-solenoid enable is on. Drive this address, not 64: a host write to 64 is overwritten on the next update. The table's key handler leaves its direct write to 64 commented out and calls de.vbs vpmKeyDown, whose swLRFlip is 82; the harness read back 64 = 1 only while 82 was held, and the ROM's ACTIVE SWITCH TEST then names RIGHT END OF STROKE #64, the manual's Lower & Upper Right Flipper Cabinet switch. The right cabinet button switches both the lower right and the upper right flipper on the 3-flipper board. The Flipper Solenoids table (PDF 40) wires each cabinet switch from the matrix drive GRN-GRY to the 3-flipper board as an ordinary switch input.

mechanisms.behavior: Six balls rest on 9 (left) to 14 (right) in the trough under the metal arch. Output 1, the lock-out, releases the ball at 14 toward the up-kicker position 15 (the ROM's 6-BALL TROUGH #7 (VUK)); output 2, the Trough Up-Kicker, lifts it into shooter lane 16. In the harness the ROM fired 1 after Start, then 2 once 15 closed. The table models the trough as a cvpmBallStack (InitSw 0,14,13,12,11,10,9,0) kicked by BallLockout and a separate BallRelease kicker at 15.
mechanisms.label: Six-ball trough and up-kicker

mechanisms.behavior: Shooter lane 16 feeds the Ball Auto Launch under the butyrate (output 3). The cabinet lever assembly "The Switch" (62) is connected with it: the skill shot is "Throw The Switch to collect value highlighted in display". In the harness the first pull of 62 with a ball at 16 fired 3; in the LASER KICK TEST a ball at 16 fired 3 without the lever.
mechanisms.label: Lever autolaunch ("The Switch")

mechanisms.behavior: A ball entering the upper scoop (with kick-big) closes 31 and output 5 kicks it out (observed in the harness gameplay run and the LASER KICK TEST).

mechanisms.behavior: A ball entering the lower scoop (with kick-big) closes 32 and output 4 kicks it out (observed in the harness gameplay run and the LASER KICK TEST).
mechanisms.label: Geneva lower scoop

mechanisms.behavior: The Ice Cave saucer at the upper left behind a 1-way gate: a ball closes 55 and output 6 ejects it (observed in the harness). The Ice Cave relights Alive.
mechanisms.label: Ice Cave ball eject

mechanisms.behavior: A ball at the North Pole closes 53 and output 7 lifts it to the upper level ramp, which carries trap doors to the creature's hands and continues as the wire ramp to the right return lane. Shooting the large ramp (45 entrance, 46 exit) lights lock; locks are made at the North Pole, and the creature "CAN HOLD 1 BALL IN EACH HAND TO THROW". Outputs 9 (right trap door) and 12 (left trap door) open the doors so a ball drops into a hand, and 13 swings both arms to throw the held balls. In the harness the ROM answered every 53 closure with 7; three ramp shots and VUK closures did not reach a lock, so the ROM's trap-door and throw sequence was not observed. The table opens trap 9 into the creature's left hand (player's right) and 12 into the right hand, and 13 throws both and closes the doors. Adjustment 51 set to NO disables the arms and the trap doors; Adjustment 52 sets the throw pulse.
mechanisms.label: North Pole VUK and creature lock

mechanisms.behavior: Output 14 moves the diverter under the ramps at the right orbit. In the harness one spin of the Ingolstadt spinner 54 fired 14. The table makes its diverter ramp collidable while 14 is on.
mechanisms.label: Right orbit ball diverter

mechanisms.behavior: When Alive is lit (lamp 33), left outlane switch 37 fires output 16, the kick back under the arch, returning the ball to play (observed in the harness gameplay run). The Ice Cave relights it. The LASER KICK TEST does not fire 16 for a closed 37 alone. Adjustment 47 starts each ball with Alive lit (MODERATE), carries it over (HARD) or starts it off (EXHARD); Adjustment 46 set to NO serves a machine without the coil, returning a lit-Alive drain to the shooter lane.
mechanisms.label: Left outlane Laser Kick

mechanisms.behavior: Top, middle left, middle right and bottom switches 41-44 fire special-solenoid outputs 17-20 within milliseconds in the harness.
mechanisms.label: Four turbo bumpers

mechanisms.behavior: Left 47 and right 48 fire outputs 21 and 22 within milliseconds in the harness.
mechanisms.label: Left and right slingshots

mechanisms.behavior: Three flippers on the solid state 3-flipper board, all 23-1100: lower left, lower right and upper right. The left cabinet button enables the lower left flipper; the right button enables both right flippers. Only the lower flippers have E.O.S. switches; the upper flipper's is printed Not Used. PinMAME copies 82/84 to matrix 64/63 and fabricates 45/46 and 47/48 in pairs, so use one state per side. No CPU driver reaches the flipper board.
mechanisms.label: Cabinet-controlled flippers

mechanisms.behavior: Output 8 pulses the knocker in the cabinet; it has no playfield sensor or placement.
mechanisms.label: Cabinet knocker

mechanisms.behavior: Relay 10 on the PPB switches drives 1-8 between the coil loads 1L-8L and the flasher loads 1R-8R (25-32). Relay 11 on the power supply board switches the G.I. supply; the table's G.I. is lit while 11 is off.
mechanisms.label: PPB bank selection and G.I. control

mechanisms.behavior: A servo motor turns the creature's head. It hangs off the Monster Head Motion Board (PN. 520-5113-00), of whose four servo outputs only #1 is used. The CPU clocks 8-bit command words to that board serially at 125 BPS with a transition-sensitive clock (four clock pulses per word) and an active-high enable, on the board's CN1-2, CN1-3 and CN1-4; each word triggers a pre-recorded routine stored in the board's micro-controller, so the CPU never positions the head itself. The servo pulse lasts 0.3 to 1.7 ms, repeats every 16.3 ms and centres the head at 1 ms. At power-up the board blinks its LED a few times and holds the servo centred until it receives a command code. The Creature Head Motion Test sends the routines from the service menu, and the manual says the motion should be the same as in game play. In the harness, public outputs 37, 38 and 44 toggled at power-up in every run and around every command of that test, 44 rising before and falling after each burst while 37 and 38 toggled. That pattern fits an enable with a clock and data pair, but no retained drawing connects the servo board to the CPU lines PinMAME publishes there, so the mechanism names no actuator. The command codes and the routine each one plays are not documented, so PinMAME's state cannot yet be mapped to a head movement. No switch reports the head's position. The retained table animates the head from its own timers (AnimateFranksHead), not from any PinMAME output.
mechanisms.label: Creature head servo

physical.notes: Driver table 1L: Coil: 6-Ball Assembly Lockout; 32v L, 25-1240. The ROM's COIL TEST prints #1L COIL: 6-BALL LOCK OUT with the wires BRN VIO-BRN and fires this address alone. Driver table 2L: Coil: Trough Up-Kicker (TRUK); 32v L, 23-800. The ROM's COIL TEST prints #2L COIL: BALL RELEASE with the wires BRN VIO-RED and fires this address alone. The Trough Up-Kicker (TRUK) lifts the ball at 15 into shooter lane 16; the location legend calls 2L "Ball Eject to Shooter Lane". In the harness it fired once 15 closed.

Driver table 3L: Coil: Auto Launch 50v; 50v L, 24-940. The ROM's COIL TEST prints #3L COIL: AUTO LAUNCH 50V with the wires YEL-VIO VIO-ORG and fires this address alone. Ball Auto Launch under the butyrate at the shooter lane, connected with the cabinet lever "The Switch" (62). In the harness the first pull of 62 with a ball at 16 fired 3. Driver table 4L: Coil: Bottom Scoop Kick-Big; 32v L, 23-800. The ROM's COIL TEST prints #4L COIL: LOWER SCOOP with the wires BRN VIO-YEL and fires this address alone. Driver table 5L: Coil: Top Scoop Kick-Big; 50v L, 23-800. The ROM's COIL TEST prints #5L COIL: UPPER SCOOP with the wires YEL-VIO VIO-GRN and fires this address alone. The Sarcophagus (upper) scoop kick-big, 50v L with the PPB helper transistor Q2. The driver table and the Tech Chart print board CPU on this row and CPU/PPB on its flasher row 5R, which uses Q42 alone; the cells are kept as printed.

Driver table 6L: Coil: Playfield Ball Eject; 32v L, 24-940. The ROM's COIL TEST prints #6L COIL: EJECT with the wires BRN VIO-BLU and fires this address alone. The North Pole vertical up-kicker lifts the ball from 53 to the upper level ramp, which carries the trap doors to the creature and continues as the wire ramp to the right return lane. The driver table and Tech Chart print coil 24-940; the coil wiring diagram prints RIGHT VUK 24-1240 and the coil chart page 25-1240, so no coil part number is asserted.

The table names this callback SolTrapLeftHand after the creature's left hand, which is on the player's right.

Driver table 10: Coil: Located on PPB in Backbox Left & Right Relay; 32v, 24v DC 10A DPDT. K1 A/B relay on the PPB in the backbox selects the 1L-8L coil loads (off) or the 1R-8R flasher loads (on) on drives 1-8. The COIL TEST selects it before every R entry and has no entry of its own.

Placements are the table's 22 G.I. bulb lights; the manual gives no complete G.I. socket list.

Driver table 12: Coil: Ramp Trap Door Left; 32v, 28-1050. The ROM's COIL TEST prints #12 COIL: LEFT TRAPDOOR with the wires RED BRN-YEL and fires this address alone. Opens the left trap door in the upper level ramp, dropping the ball into the creature's right hand on the player's left.

Driver table 13: Coil: Monster Arms; 32v, 23-800. The ROM's COIL TEST prints #13 COIL: CREATURE THROW with the wires RED BRN-GRN and fires this address alone. Adjustment 51 Enable Creature Throw set to NO disables the arms and the trap doors, and Adjustment 52 sets the throw pulse. The five service-test runs, booted with an empty trough, saw the ROM pulse 13 once about 3.8 s after power-up; the gameplay run, booted with six balls in the trough, did not. The Tech Chart prints Monster Arms 50v with Q26/Q3 on PPB J 8-7 (VIO-YEL, PPB J 7-3); the manual's driver table, the coil wiring diagram (MONSTER ARMS 23-800 on CPU CN12-6) and the ROM's RED power wire agree on 32v from the power supply, which this record follows.

Driver table 14: Coil: Right Orbit Ball Diverter; 32v, 27-1400. The ROM's COIL TEST prints #14 COIL: DIVERTER with the wires BRN-BLU VIO-YEL and fires this address alone. The ROM's other entries print the power wire first and the control wire second; here it prints BRN-BLU VIO-YEL, where the driver table prints power RED and control BRN-BLU, which this record follows.
